Here's the script. Hook archetype: **specific number / contrarian** — the real cost driver wasn't the obvious one. Structure: **myth / correction**, which pairs with that hook and plays well on LinkedIn where a concrete, counterintuitive number beats general advice.

---

## Hook (first 3 seconds)

**On-screen text:** "Our second café cost 40% more than our first."
**Spoken:** "Our second location cost 40% more than the first — and rent had almost nothing to do with it."

*Visual: you, to camera, in the new space. Text sits mid-frame, clear of the top 14% and bottom 20%.*

---

## Body (3-4 scenes with cues)

**Scene 1 — the assumption (0:03–0:12)**
*Cue: cut to the lease paperwork or the new storefront.*
"We budgeted like a rent problem. Bigger city, higher rent — we padded for that and thought we were covered."

**Scene 2 — the correction (0:12–0:28)**
*Cue: cut to the floor — baristas training, not serving.*
"Rent came in about 10% over the first site. Staffing came in at nearly double. The first location was built around people we'd worked with for years. The second one, we were hiring and training from zero — six weeks of paid shifts before anyone was fast enough to run a bar solo."

**Scene 3 — the real cost (0:28–0:42)**
*Cue: on-screen line — "The 40% was onboarding, not overhead."*
"That ramp-up — overlapping shifts, slower service, mistakes we ate the cost of — that was the 40%. Not the building. The time it takes a new team to become a team."

**Scene 4 — the lesson (0:42–0:55)**
*Cue: back to camera.*
"If we open a third, the training budget gets written first and the rent gets written second. We had it backwards."

---

## CTA

*Spoken + on-screen, before the final frame:*
"If you've opened a second site — was your biggest surprise on the P&L the one you expected, or the one you didn't? Curious whether staffing caught others out too."

*Final frame: loop back to the new storefront with the opening text.*

---

**Caption first line (the second hook):** "Rent was 10% over budget. Staffing was nearly double. Here's what opening our second café actually taught us."

Put any link to the new location in the **first comment**, not the post body — external links in the body cut LinkedIn reach.

One note: swap the "40% more" and "nearly double" figures for your real numbers before posting — a specific, true figure is the whole engine of this hook, and a round estimate reads as invented.
